t.4.40.1: Then Sugrīva, having dispatched that great army of monkeys, sent chosen monkeys toward the southern quarter.
t.4.40.2: Nīla, the son of Agni, and the monkey Hanumān, and Jāmbavān, the son of the Grandfather, the great monkey.
t.4.40.3: Suhotra and Śarāri, and likewise Śaragulma, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Suṣeṇa, and Ṛṣabha as well.
t.4.40.5: The heroic lord of the monkey hosts, who knew the distinctions of things, instructed the heroes headed by Aṅgada, who were endowed with speed and valour.
t.4.40.4: Mainda and Dvivida as well, Vijaya and Gandhamādana, Ulkāmukha and Asaṅga, the two sons of Hutāśana,
t.4.40.6: Having arranged a great army of monkey heroes, moving without hindrance, to go ahead of them, he directed it toward the southern quarter.
t.4.40.7: Whatever regions there were in that direction, all of them very hard to reach, the lord of the monkeys described them all to those chief monkeys.
t.4.40.8: Search the thousand-peaked Vindhya, covered with many kinds of trees and creepers, and the river Narmadā, difficult of access and frequented by great serpents.
t.4.40.9: Then search the delightful Godāvarī, the great river Kṛṣṇaveṇī, and the most blessed Varadā, frequented by great serpents.
t.4.40.10: Search the Mekhalas and the Utkalas, and the cities of the Daśārṇas too, Avantī and Abhravantī; look over all of them thoroughly.
t.4.40.11: Search the Vidarbhas, the Ṛṣikas, and the delightful Māhiṣakas as well, and likewise the Vaṅgas, the Kaliṅgas and the Kauśikas on every side.
t.4.40.13: Likewise you must go to the Andhras, the Puṇḍras, the Colas and the Pāṇḍyas together with the Keralas, and also to Mount Ayomukha, adorned with minerals.
t.4.40.12: Having scanned the Daṇḍaka forest with its mountains, rivers and caves, and the river Godāvarī as well, search through everything thoroughly.
t.4.40.14: The great mountain, splendid, with its variegated peaks, its forests bright with many-coloured blossoms, and its regions of sandalwood groves, must be searched.
t.4.40.15: Then there you will see that divine river Kāverī, auspicious and with clear waters, where hosts of Apsarases sport.
t.4.40.16: On the summit of that mountain Malaya you will see Agastya, the best of sages, seated there, mighty in splendour and resembling the sun.
t.4.40.17: Then, permitted by that gracious great-souled one, you shall cross the great river Tāmraparṇī, which is frequented by crocodiles.
t.4.40.19: Then, O Vānaras, having gone there you will see the gate of the Pāṇḍyas, golden, divine, adorned with pearls and jewels, and fitting.
t.4.40.18: That river, veiled by heavenly sandalwood forests and graced with islands, plunges into the ocean as a lovely young woman goes to her beloved.
t.4.40.21: There stands the glorious Mahendra, foremost of mountains, adorned with many wondrous trees, made of gold and resplendent, plunging deep into the great ocean.
t.4.40.20: Then, having reached the ocean and firmly settled on your purpose, you will find there one who was placed by Agastya in the midst of that sea.
t.4.40.22: That mountain is adorned with flowering trees of many kinds and with creepers, and is frequented by the foremost of gods, seers and Yakṣas, and by Apsarases.
t.4.40.23: That exceedingly charming mountain, thronged with hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas, is ever visited by the thousand-eyed Sahasrākṣa on each and every festival day.
t.4.40.24: On its farther shore lies an island, a hundred yojanas in extent, radiant and inaccessible to men; search it on every side. There above all Sītā must be sought with your whole being.
t.4.40.25: For that region is indeed the abode of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, who is doomed to be slain and whose splendour equals that of the thousand-eyed Indra.
t.4.40.26: In the middle of that southern ocean dwells a rākṣasī, famed by the name Aṅgārakā, who seizes the shadows of creatures and devours them.
t.4.40.27: Beyond that, in the ocean a hundred yojanas wide, lies a splendid mountain named Puṣpitaka, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
t.4.40.28: Resembling the rays of the moon and the sun, encircled by the waters of the ocean, it shines with its vast peaks, as though scratching the sky.
t.4.40.29: Of that mountain, there is one golden peak to which the sun resorts, and one white peak of silver to which the moon resorts.
t.4.40.30: The ungrateful do not see it, nor do the cruel, nor the unbelievers. Bowing your heads to that mountain, search it, O monkeys.
t.4.40.32: Then, having passed beyond that too, there is the mountain named Vaidyuta, with trees bearing fruits that fulfil every desire and delightful in every season.
t.4.40.31: Having passed beyond it, you invincible ones, after fourteen yojanas along a path hard to traverse, there is the mountain named Sūryavān.
t.4.40.33: There, O monkeys, having eaten roots and fruits worthy of the best, and having drunk the finest honey, go on farther.
t.4.40.34: There stands the mountain named Kuñjara, delightful to the eyes and the mind, where the abode of Agastya was built by Viśvakarman.
t.4.40.35: There stands a divine golden abode, one yojana in breadth and ten yojanas high, adorned with many kinds of jewels.
t.4.40.36: There lies the city named Bhogavatī, the dwelling of the serpents, with broad streets, unassailable and guarded on every side, protected by fearsome serpents with sharp fangs and deadly venom.
t.4.40.37: Having gone forth, you must also search that city Bhogavatī, in which dwells Vāsuki, the king of serpents, exceedingly terrible.
t.4.40.38: Beyond that region stands a great mountain named Ṛṣabha, shaped like a bull, splendid and made entirely of every kind of gem.
t.4.40.40: But having seen that sandalwood, you must never touch it at any time, for fearsome Gandharvas named Rohitas guard that forest.
t.4.40.39: There, where divine sandalwood grows, the gośīrṣaka, the padmaka and the greenish-dark kind, that too shines with a splendour like fire.
t.4.40.41: There dwell the five lords of the Gandharvas, whose splendour equals that of the sun: Śailūṣa, Grāmaṇī, Bhikṣu, Śubhra, and likewise Babhru.
t.4.40.42: There, at the end of the earth, dwell the invincible ones who have conquered heaven. Beyond that lies the most dreadful world of the ancestors, which you must not approach; this is the royal city of Yama, shrouded in grievous darkness.
t.4.40.43: O heroes, bulls among the vānaras, only this far is it possible for you to search or to go; beyond this there is no passage even for those who are able to move.
t.4.40.44: Having surveyed all this, and whatever else may also be seen, and having learned the whereabouts of Vaidehī, you should return.
t.4.40.45: He who returns within a month and is the first to say, "Sītā has been seen," shall live happily, enjoying pleasures, with splendour equal to my own.
t.4.40.46: Then no one is dearer to me, dearer even than my own life; though he may have committed offences many times, he will become my kinsman.
t.4.40.47: You are of immeasurable strength and valour, and you are born in families of abundant virtues. Undertake, then, that surpassing manly effort by which you may obtain the daughter of the lord of men.
